summary.text: Bruce Roy is a retired Air National Guard colonel and IBM engineer who is the Republican candidate for the Vermont State Senate in the Chittenden Southeast District in the November 3, 2026 general election.

He ran for the same seat in 2024 and for the Vermont House in 2022, and in a Ballotpedia survey he said he supports Governor Phil Scott's affordability agenda and wants to control government spending and the tax burden.

paragraphs.text: Bruce Roy said in a Ballotpedia survey that he is a long-time Vermonter who graduated from Essex Junction High School and the University of Vermont, and that he served four years on active duty in the U.S. Air Force.
He then joined IBM as an engineer while continuing to serve in the Vermont Air National Guard, and he said he had 30-year careers at both, retiring as a colonel in 2008 and from IBM in 2013.
He also described serving on the Essex School Board and teaching for ten years at the Community College of Vermont, and said he has lived in Williston since 2001.
Roy was the Republican candidate for the Vermont House Chittenden 2 District in 2022, finishing third with 17.4 percent in a two-seat race won by Erin Brady and Angela Arsenault.
In 2024 he ran for the three-seat Chittenden Southeast State Senate district and received 15.0 percent of the vote, behind the three Democratic winners.

In his 2026 survey he listed priorities including education finance reform, a lower tax burden, controlled government spending, business growth and a reasonable and affordable approach to environmental protection, and he named Governor Phil Scott and former Governor Jim Douglas as endorsers.
